The story unfolds entirely in real-time through a dialogue-driven scene, meaning "story time" and "real world time" are virtually identical. Rather than stretching out the scene with lengthy internal monologues or compressing the conversation into a summary, the writer relies on brief, loaded exchanges and small physical cues (like stirring an already-stirred coffee, keeping a jacket on, and then slightly unzipping it) to control the rhythm. At the same time, the shared history and years of estrangement between Jonas and Martin are effectively compressed into subtext and a few short lines of dialogue. This balanced pacing makes the awkward tension and the gradual, subtle thawing between the two characters feel completely natural and earned.
